# Purpose

This document explains the intended workflow of `sales_summary.R`[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span). The script reads a synthetic retail CSV file, validates expected columns, and summarizes units and sales value by product category and region[span_4](start_span)[span_4](end_span).

## Inputs

- `retail_sales.csv`: synthetic transaction-level data[span_5](start_span)[span_5](end_span).
- Required columns: `order_id`, `date`, `category`, `region`, `units`, and `unit_price`[span_6](start_span)[span_6](end_span).

## Outputs

- A grouped summary containing category, region, total units, and total sales[span_7](start_span)[span_7](end_span).

## Dependencies

Uses `readr` for importing CSV files and `dplyr` for data transformation[span_8](start_span)[span_8](end_span).

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
Example Workflow
​1. Read the input data

sales_data <- read_csv("retail_sales.csv")

2. Check the required columns
required_columns <- c(
  "order_id", "date", "category",
  "region", "units", "unit_price"
)

stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(sales_data)))
3. Create the summary
sales_summary <- sales_data %>%
  group_by(category, region) %>%
  summarise(
    total_units = sum(units, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_sales = sum(units * unit_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
4. Review the output
print(sales_summary)

Validation Notes
​Confirmed CSV file format and column names.
​Checked data types for date, units, and unit_price.
​Inspected missing values.
​Successfully knitted the .Rmd file in RStudio.
